clue.text: Record middle section of prom fortissimo; gradually fade away

parts.note: to record on a cassette is to tape

indicators.note: asks for the central letters of the word prom, dropping its first and last

parts.note: ff is the musical score marking for fortissimo, very loud

explanation.surface: A concert-goer notes the loudest stretch of a Proms concert before the music dies away.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'prom' is a Proms concert (London's summer classical series) in the surface; here only its middle letters RO are used.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwindle or diminish bit by bit is the phrasal-verb sense of fading away gradually.

clue.text: Looking up title of painting encircling tin — 'Change'

indicators.note: in a down clue looking up means the whole assembly is read from bottom to top
the title-of-painting string goes round the symbol for tin

parts.note: Mr is a man's courtesy title
taken as written
painting is a form of art
Sn is the chemical symbol for tin

explanation.surface: A gallery visitor glances up at a painting's label mentioning tin and the word Change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Encircling' puts SN between MROF and ART to give MROFSNART; 'Looking up' then reads that string backwards, from the bottom of the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter something completely is to convert it, the verb sense of change.

clue.text: Rivet pear shaped for old ship

indicators.note: the letters of rivet and pear are formed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A metalworker hammers a rivet into a pear shape to make a model of an old vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shaped' rearranges RIVET and PEAR together.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically, a privately owned armed vessel licensed by a government to attack enemy shipping is an example of an old ship.

clue.text: Taking extract of curare? Ear-throbbing is an element

indicators.note: signals that a run of letters is lifted out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone poisoned with curare feels their ears throbbing and wonders which element is to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: Curare is a South American arrow poison; the run sits across its last letters, 'Ear' and the start of 'throbbing'.
explanation.definitionFit: The lanthanides such as cerium and neodymium are a group of metallic chemical elements, so one of them is an element.

clue.text: If hale, her art not right, somehow, for such a person

indicators.note: says the letters of the phrase before it are mixed in some unspecified way
signals that the letter for right is left out of the phrase before the mixing

parts.note: the fodder taken as written, its punctuation ignored

explanation.surface: Someone hale but with a failing heart turns to a particular kind of practitioner.
explanation.walkthrough: IFHALEHERART has an R too many: 'not right' takes it out, and 'somehow' shuffles the remaining eleven letters. The surface's healthy person with a bad heart suits the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who claims to cure illness through prayer or belief rather than medicine is described by 'such a person' read with the surface.

clue.text: A loving touch 1. troubles start to subside

parts.note: worries or troubles are cares

indicators.note: takes just the opening letter of the word subside

explanation.surface: A gentle embrace makes your worries begin to ebb away.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle stroke given with affection is a loving touch.

clue.text: Family's good, sound

parts.note: a clan is a family group; the apostrophe-s adds no letters

explanation.surface: A remark that a family is in good health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning healthy, matching 'good'; it is the noun for a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud ringing metallic noise is a kind of sound.

clue.text: Train boarded — it's necessary to make tracks

indicators.note: to train something is to direct or shape it, so the letters of boarded are re-formed

explanation.surface: Passengers have got on a train, and the next step is to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like the noun for railway carriages; it is the anagram signal, and 'make tracks' looks like leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: The foundation of gravel and earth on which railway sleepers and rails are laid is what is needed to build railway lines.

clue.text: Fluttering kilts if it's used in the Cairngorms

indicators.note: flapping about suggests the letters of kilts and if are blown into a new order

explanation.surface: Kilts flap in the wind up in the Scottish mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cairngorms are a mountain range in the Scottish Highlands with ski resorts; kilts belong to the same Scottish picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable-driven conveyor that carries skiers uphill is a piece of equipment found at Scottish ski centres such as Cairngorm.

clue.text: Current by island to carry off corrosive liquid

parts.note: AC is alternating current
to drain liquid is to carry it off

explanation.surface: A current flowing past an island washes away some corrosive substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Precipitation made acidic by pollution is a damaging, corrosive form of water.

clue.text: Slow in scoring

parts.note: read as a tempo instruction written on a musical score, not as a team being slow to get points

explanation.definitionFit: An Italian tempo direction meaning at a leisurely pace appears on sheet music to mark a slow movement.

clue.text: Criticise sides of shoe, pinching muscle

indicators.note: the shoe's outer letters grip the muscle word between them
takes the first and last letters of shoe

parts.note: lat is short for latissimus dorsi, the broad back muscle

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the sides of their shoe are pinching a muscle in the foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sides of' takes S and E from 'shoe', and 'pinching' puts LAT between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To slate a play or book is a British informal verb for attacking it harshly in a review.

clue.text: Limpin' round turn shows little spirit

indicators.note: the limping word goes round the word for a turn

parts.note: hobblin' is limping, with the same dropped g
a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: Someone limping round a bend reveals a small ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' puts GO inside HOBBLIN, splitting it after HOB.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischievous imp of folklore is a small sprite or goblin, so a diminutive supernatural being.

clue.text: Collector's protection against lion and crocodile, one hears

indicators.note: says the pieces are spoken and the answer is what they sound like

parts.note: a bib is protection, Leo the zodiac lion and a crocodile a school file of pupils walking in line; against sets them side by side, said BIB-LEO-FILE

explanation.surface: A naturalist's kit for protection against a lion and a crocodile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crocodile' here is the British school term for children walking in a double line, so a file. Said together, BIB-LEO-FILE gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who loves and amasses books is a book collector.

clue.text: You're not likely to get flush by pulling their handles

definitions.text: You're not likely to get flush by pulling their handles

parts.words: You're not likely to get flush by pulling their handles
parts.note: flush reads as a poker hand or as being well off with money; pulling the lever of a fruit machine rarely makes you rich

explanation.definitionFit: Slot machines in arcades are operated by a single lever on the side, and they rarely pay out much.

clue.text: Casual, flimsy garment, short mantle essentially

indicators.note: the garment's name is cut by its final letter

parts.note: a negligee is a light, sheer dressing gown

indicators.note: takes the core letters of mantle, its middle two

explanation.surface: A thin nightdress paired with a cropped cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' trims NEGLIGEE to NEGLIGE, and 'essentially' gives NT, the centre of 'mantle'.
explanation.definitionFit: Careless or offhand in attention to duty is a sense of casual.

clue.text: Emphasise in print it is in girl's possession

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: together with possession, says the girl's name holds the next word
with in, says the girl's name has the word is inside it

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name; the apostrophe-s adds nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something is owned by a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In girl's possession' puts IS inside ALICE, after ALIC, and IT comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting words in sloping type is a typographic way to stress them on the page.

clue.text: Duke takes part of National Trust in thoughts for grounds

indicators.note: D takes on the role or place of the letters for National Trust

parts.note: sentiments are thoughts or feelings
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: A duke joins a National Trust property in his reflections.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British charity that looks after historic houses. 'Takes part of' means D plays NT's part, replacing it in SENTIMENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee grounds are the dregs left in the cup, matter that settles at the bottom.

clue.text: Coaches may be excluded in track events here

definitions.text: Coaches may be excluded in track events here

parts.words: Coaches may be excluded in track events here
parts.note: coaches and track read as athletics trainers at a race meeting, but they are railway carriages being sorted on lines

explanation.definitionFit: A railway sidings area where carriages and wagons are sorted and assembled into trains.

clue.text: Placate primate, picking up first of parson's errors and swearing

indicators.note: the primate word collects the following letters inside itself

parts.note: an ape is a primate

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: A monkey copies a vicar's mistakes and bad language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First of' applies to all four words, giving PEAS, which 'picking up' puts inside APE after its A and P.
explanation.definitionFit: To pacify someone by meeting their demands is to placate them.

clue.text: Woman to ring up and record material

parts.note: she refers to a woman

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for ring is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them

explanation.surface: A woman phones to arrange a recording session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' turns CALL into LLAC after SHE. The definition is 'record material': old 78 rpm records were made of this resin.
explanation.definitionFit: A resin from the lac insect was the substance from which early gramophone discs were pressed.

clue.text: Rich in tears about police check

indicators.note: says the assembled letters are turned round and read backwards
the word for rich goes inside the word for tears

parts.note: parts is tears, as in tears asunder
deep means rich, as of a colour or voice

explanation.surface: A wealthy person sobs about being stopped by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts DEEP inside PARTS to give PARTDEEPS, and 'about' reverses it. 'Tears' is the verb that rhymes with 'bears', not crying.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of road where officers monitor motorists' velocity is a roadside enforcement check.

clue.text: Giant bird getting a baboon finally

parts.note: a tit is a small bird

indicators.note: takes the closing letter of baboon

explanation.surface: A large bird gets a baboon at last.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Titans were a race of huge gods, so the word names any colossus.

clue.text: Woman bowled over on island, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: knocked flat, so the woman's name is turned backwards

parts.note: Di is a woman's name
IOM is the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A woman is knocked off her feet while on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowled over' turns DI into ID; then IOM follows. 'In' is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: An expression whose meaning is fixed by usage rather than by its words is a characteristic turn of phrase.

clue.text: Big hitter fifty-fifty to get into side when returning

indicators.note: says the letters built so far are read backwards
the fifty-fifty letters go inside the word for side

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two of them

explanation.surface: A heavy hitter takes an even share of the runs for his side on the way back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To get into' puts LL in TEAM, giving TELLAM, and 'when returning' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden hammer, as used in croquet or by a carpenter, is a tool for striking hard.

clue.text: African left nearest bit of Europe before noon

parts.note: Iberia, the Spain-Portugal peninsula, is the part of Europe closest to Africa

explanation.surface: An African set out for Spain and Portugal before midday.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Liberia, a West African republic, is a person from that continent.

clue.text: Old teacher in talk about light

indicators.note: says the word for the teacher is spoken, giving letters that match its sound

parts.note: beak is old British school slang for a schoolmaster
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: An old schoolmaster gives a lecture about light.
explanation.walkthrough: BEAK is dated British slang for a teacher or magistrate; spoken, it is the first part of the answer, then ON for 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal fire or lighthouse is a warning light.

clue.text: Struggles without wife and son, unable to sleep

indicators.note: the word for wife is removed from the word for struggles

parts.note: to wrestle is to struggle

explanation.surface: Someone fights on alone without their wife and son and cannot sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' takes W from WRESTLES, leaving RESTLES, and S is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Tossing and turning, never settling into slumber, describes a fidgety, wakeful state.
